Check out the pull request's head for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102 and run every check there from the repository root. Run `npm ci` first. Make temp files in a scratch directory outside the repo (e.g. `mktemp -d`). One check per expect line, in order.

Check 1 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none".
Run: create `clean.jsonl` with `{"a":1}\n{"b":2}\n`; run `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $T/clean.jsonl; echo $?`. Create `bad.jsonl` with content `{"a":1}\n\n{bad\n   \n{"c":3}\n{"d":` (printf, no trailing newline: line 2 blank, line 3 invalid, line 4 whitespace-only, line 5 valid, line 6 unterminated and invalid); run the bin on it and capture stdout and exit code. Also run it on a file whose only content is `{"a":1}` with no trailing newline (expect exit 0, no output).
PASS: clean file → exit 0, no error lines on stdout; bad file → stdout has exactly two finding lines, one starting `$T/bad.jsonl:3: ` and one starting `$T/bad.jsonl:6: `, each followed by a non-empty error text, no lines for blank lines 2 and 4 or valid line 5, exit code 1; the valid unterminated single-row file → exit 0.
FAIL: any wrong or missing line number, a line reported for a blank row, the unterminated last row not reported, output not in `<file>:<line>: <error>` form, or a wrong exit code.

Check 2 — expect: "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2".
Run: `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $T/does-not-exist.jsonl >out 2>err; echo $?` and `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js >out 2>err; echo $?`.
PASS: both exit 2 and each `err` is non-empty.
FAIL: any other exit code, or nothing written to stderr, in either case.

Check 3 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]".
Run: `node --input-type=module -e "import {lint} from './packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js'; console.log(JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n\n{bad\n{\"b\":')), JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n')))"`.
PASS: `lint` is an exported function; the first result is an array of two objects with `line` 3 and 4 respectively, each with a `line` number and a string `error`; the second result is `[]`.
FAIL: import fails, `lint` is not exported, the return is not an array of `{ line, error }` objects, or the lines are wrong.

Check 4 — expect: "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes".
Run: read `packages/jsonl-lint/package.json`; run `npm test -w jsonl-lint` and `cd packages/jsonl-lint && node --test`; read the test files under `packages/jsonl-lint`.
PASS: package.json has `name` `jsonl-lint`, `type` `module`, `scripts.test` `node --test`, and no `dependencies` (absent or empty); the tests import from `node:test`, run, and pass with zero failures; the test files contain tests that exercise a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn (unterminated, invalid) last row, blank lines, and the CLI exit codes (0, 1 and 2).
FAIL: any of those fields wrong, any runtime dependency, any failing test, or any of the five listed test cases missing.

Check 5 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool".
Run: `test -s packages/jsonl-lint/README.md && echo ok`; `grep -n jsonl-lint README.md`.
PASS: the package README exists and is non-empty, and the root `README.md` mentions jsonl-lint as a tool in the repo.
FAIL: package README missing/empty, or root README does not list the tool.

Check 6 — expect: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head".
